newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada issues deportation order on Saudi suspect.
newsitem.headline: Canada issues deportation order on Saudi suspect.

text.p: The Canadian government issued a conditional order on Wednesday for the deportation of a Saudi man wanted by the United States for alleged involvement in a bombing that killed 19 U.S. airmen in Saudi Arabia last June.

An immigration official said that once the government decided where to send Hani Abdel-Rahim Hussein al-Sayegh, it would be a formality to deport him from Canada. The leading choices are Saudi Arabia and the United States.

"We are certainly going to pursue this to deport him as quickly and efficiently as we can," David Olson, a Canadian citizenship official, told reporters inside an Ottawa prison after adjudicator G.R. McBrien signed the order.

Canada's Federal Court ruled on May 5 that a security certificate declaring that Sayegh was a terrorist and a danger to Canada was reasonable, but Wednesday's 11-minute hearing was required to issue the deportation order.
Canadian authorities had accused him of being a driver in the massive truck bombing on June 25 at the Khobar Towers, a complex housing U.S. military personnel in Dhahran, in eastern Saudi Arabia.

Sayegh's lawyer, Doug Baum, said he would press Citizenship and Immigration Minister Lucienne Robillard not to send him to Saudi Arabia, on the grounds that he could well be tortured and executed without a fair trial.
